resources.heroDesc: Everything a dealer, contractor, or project engineer needs to spec and install Poddar Pipes products correctly.
resources.installLink: Looking for the step-by-step installation process? See the Installation Guide

installation.heroDesc: The same 6-step solvent-weld process used across Poddar's uPVC, CPVC, SWR, UGD, and Agri Gold catalogues — step through it below, or jump to handling, storage, and site-condition guidance.
installation.step0Desc: Measure the required pipe length and mark it clearly using a felt tip pen. Verify size compatibility before proceeding. Cut using a plywood saw, ratchet cutter, or wheel cutter, always at 90° to ensure an optimal bonding area. Inspect pipe ends thoroughly before jointing — if any crack or splintering is found, cut a minimum of 25mm beyond the visible damage before proceeding.
installation.step1Desc: Burrs on or inside the pipe end can obstruct flow and prevent proper contact between the pipe and fitting socket. Remove them carefully from both inner and outer surfaces using a 15mm half-round file, pen knife, or deburring tool. Applying a slight bevel to the pipe end eases its entry into the fitting socket during assembly.
installation.step2Desc: Wipe all dirt, dust, and moisture thoroughly from the fitting sockets and pipe end using a clean, dry rag. Perform a dry fit to confirm the pipe enters fully and reaches the bottom of the socket without obstruction. Once confirmed, mark the pipe clearly at the socket entry point using a felt tip pen for accurate reference during final assembly.
installation.step3Desc: Use only genuine Poddar solvent cement conforming to ASTM D-2564 / IS 14182 for a reliable solvent weld joint. Apply a smooth, even coat uniformly across the pipe end and inside the fitting socket. Never use thickened or lumpy cement — it must flow freely with a consistency similar to syrup or paint for proper surface penetration.
installation.step4Desc: Immediately after applying solvent cement, insert the pipe firmly into the fitting socket. Rotate the pipe a quarter to half turn while inserting to distribute the cement evenly across the joint surface. Hold the assembly firmly in position for a minimum of 3 seconds to allow the joint to begin setting and prevent push-out.
installation.step5Desc: Check that a continuous bead of solvent cement has formed around the full circumference of the socket fitting entrance, confirming sufficient cement coverage and a fully sealed joint. Using a clean, dry cloth, wipe away excess solvent cement from the external surface of both the pipe and fitting for a clean, professional finish.
installation.handling0Desc: Thoroughly inspect every pipe for signs of transit damage — cracks, chips, or shifts in load — before accepting delivery or proceeding with installation.
installation.handling1Desc: Never throw, drop, or drag pipes from a truck bed or elevated surface, and keep them away from sharp objects and edges at all times.
installation.handling2Desc: Store pipes indoors where possible, on a level, dry surface, shielded from direct sunlight to minimise UV exposure.
installation.handling3Desc: Position thicker-walled pipes at the bottom of the stack. If stored on racks, keep support spacing under 3 feet to prevent bowing.
installation.handling4Title: Seal solvent cement after every use
installation.handling4Desc: Replace and tighten the container lid immediately after each application to prevent evaporation and fume escape.
installation.handling5Desc: Avoid inhaling solvent vapours for extended periods — maintain ventilation throughout the jointing process, especially in enclosed areas.
installation.handling6Desc: Prevent direct contact with solvent cement. If eye contact occurs, flush thoroughly with clean water for at least 15 minutes and seek medical attention.
installation.handling7Desc: Keep solvent cement, primers, and cleaners tightly sealed except during active use, and dispose of used rags responsibly.
installation.handling8Desc: Store and use solvent cement well away from open flames, heat sources, sparks, and combustion-triggering equipment.
installation.hotWeatherTip0: Store solvent cement in a cool or well-shaded location prior to use to maintain its consistency and effectiveness.
installation.hotWeatherTip1: Where possible, store pipes and fittings in a shaded area before applying solvent cement to prevent surfaces from becoming too warm.
installation.hotWeatherTip2: Cool down the surfaces to be joined using a clean, damp rag before beginning — ensure the surface is completely dry before applying solvent cement.
installation.hotWeatherTip3: Where possible, carry out solvent cement application during the cooler morning hours to allow better working time.
installation.hotWeatherTip4: Always confirm that both surfaces being joined are still visibly wet with solvent cement at the moment they are brought together.
installation.hotWeatherTip5: Vigorously stir or shake the solvent cement container thoroughly before each use to ensure a uniform consistency.
installation.hotWeatherTip6: Complete system anchoring and final pipe connections during the cooler parts of the day to account for thermal expansion and contraction.
installation.warning0: Always perform a complete dry fit of all joints prior to applying any solvent cement, to confirm a proper and secure interference fit exists between components.
installation.warning1: Any fitting joint that does not demonstrate a correct interference fit during dry fitting must be discarded and replaced immediately.
installation.warning2: Do NOT apply solvent cement to any joint that feels either too loose or excessively tight — improper fit results in a weak or failed joint.
installation.warning3: Always use appropriate, purpose-made bevelling tools to correctly prepare all pipe ends before any solvent cement is applied.
installation.warning4: Do NOT apply solvent cement to any joint without first completing the bevelling of all pipe ends.
installation.warning5: Use only One-Step solvent cement when connecting all pipes, fittings, and accessories, to ensure a consistently strong, leak-proof joint.
installation.warning6: Do NOT use any primer in combination with One-Step solvent cement — primer is neither required nor compatible with this jointing system.
installation.warning7: Do NOT use any other brand or type of solvent cement to connect Poddar pipes, fittings, and accessories, as this may result in joint failure.

faq.heading: Answers before you reach out.
faq.desc: Can't find what you're looking for? Send us a message and a team member will follow up directly.
faq.q0: What product categories does Poddar Pipes manufacture?
faq.a0: We manufacture uPVC, CPVC, SWR, UGD, and Agriculture piping systems, along with rotomoulded water storage TANKS, plus a full range of fittings, valves, and accessories.
faq.q1: Are Poddar Pipes products BIS/ISI certified?
faq.a1: Our pipe ranges are manufactured to relevant Indian Standards (IS 13592, IS 14735, IS 15778, IS 16098) with ISI marking as applicable to each product category.
faq.q2: How do I set up a business partnership or distribution agreement with Poddar Pipes?
faq.a2: Submit a business enquiry through the Contact page with your business details and territory of interest. Our regional sales team will follow up to discuss requirements and terms.
faq.q3: Do you provide technical support for large infrastructure projects?
faq.a3: Yes, our engineering team supports project specification, on-site installation guidance, and commissioning support for municipal, industrial, and irrigation infrastructure projects.
faq.q4: Where can I download product datasheets and catalogues?
faq.a4: All product datasheets, brochures, and installation manuals are available in the Resources section, organized by product category.
faq.q5: Do you offer bulk pricing for large orders?
faq.a5: Yes, bulk and project pricing is available. Please submit a quote request through the Contact page with your estimated volume and project timeline.
faq.a6: A lead-free water supply system is the safest and most preferred choice for potable water transportation worldwide. Eliminating lead from the pipe compound ensures the water conveyed remains completely uncontaminated and safe for human consumption.
faq.a7: UV resistance prevents the oxidation process that occurs upon prolonged sunlight exposure, protecting the material from degradation and significantly extending the durability and service life of pipes and fittings installed outdoors.
faq.q8: How are Poddar pipes and fittings aligned during installation?
faq.a8: Elbows and fittings in common sizes carry an alignment mould mark that lines up with a coloured stripe on the pipe during solvent cement jointing, keeping outlet fittings perpendicular to the wall in concealed installations — especially useful in unplastered walls with no other reference surface.
faq.q9: What about health, safety, and fire toxicity?
faq.a9: Independent testing confirms uPVC performs better than metal-based piping systems in terms of its effect on water quality, and is no more toxic than wood in fire conditions. With a Limiting Oxygen Index of 45, uPVC is effectively non-combustible under normal atmospheric conditions and stops burning as soon as the external ignition source is removed.
faq.q10: What does the product warranty cover?
faq.a10: Poddar Pipes warrants that products will remain free from manufacturing defects and conform to applicable BIS standards under normal operating conditions. The remedy is limited to replacement of, or credit for, the defective product — it doesn't cover removal/reinstallation labour, and doesn't apply if mixed with another brand's pipes/fittings/solvent cement, if joints weren't pressure-tested before plastering, or if damage results from drilling, chiselling, or other mechanical interference after installation.
